sentences.text: HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD ?Court No. - 84 Case :- CRIMINAL MISC ANTICIPATORY BAIL APPLICATION U/S 438 CR.P.C. No. - 3170 of 2023 Applicant :- Smt Gulshana Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Applicant :- Alok Kumar Singh Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Sunil Kumar Dubey Hon'ble Nalin Kumar Srivastava,J.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State as well as learned counsel for the informant and perused the record.

This application has been moved on behalf of the applicant Smt. Gulshana seeking anticipatory bail in Case Crime No.740 of 2022 under Sections 498-A, 323, 504, 506, 328, 304-B IPC and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Muradnagar, District Ghaziabad.

It has been submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is innocent and she has apprehension of her arrest in the above-mentioned case, whereas there is no credible evidence against her.
Allegations levelled against the applicant are false.
Applicant's case is squarely covered under Section 438 Cr.P.C.
If the applicant is enlarged on anticipatory bail, she will not misuse the liberty and will cooperate with the investigation.
The applicant has apprehension of her arrest by the police any time.
Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer and submitted that sufficient evidence has been collected against the applicant, which shows the involvement of the applicant in the present matter.
Offences levelled against the applicant are of serious nature.

Continuously, she is absconding and not cooperating Smt Gulshana vs State Of U.P. And Another on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150516114/
1 with the investigation.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that process under Section 82 Cr.P.C. has been issued against the present applicant, which means that she has been declared as proclaimed absconder by the Court.
In this connection, an F.I.R. under Section 174-A IPC has also been lodged against her on 11.4.2023.
From the perusal of record, it appears that the applicant had been absconding throughout and process under Section 82 Cr.P.C. was issued against her.
The conduct of the applicant falls within the ambit of the law promulgated by Hon'ble Apex Court in Prem Shankar Prasad Versus State of Bihar and Another, 2021 SCC OnLine Supreme Court 955.

entities.text: Prem Shankar Prasad Versus State of Bihar and Another, 2021 SCC OnLine Supreme Court 955
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the facts of the case, charge-sheet was filed under Sections 406, 420 IPC against the accused and thus it was explicit that a prima facie case against the accused was found.

From the record, it reveals that the arrest warrant was issued by the Magistrate against the accused and thereafter proceedings under Sections 82, 83 Cr.P.C. had been initiated pursuant to the order passed by the Magistrate.
Only thereafter the accused moved an application before the trial court for anticipatory bail, which was rejected by the Sessions Court.
However, subsequently anticipatory bail was granted to the aforesaid accused by the High Court and when the matter came before the Hon'ble Apex Court, it was observed like this.

"19. Despite the above observations on merits and despite the fact that it was brought to the notice of the High Court that respondent No. 2 - accused is absconding and even the proceedings under sections 82-83 of Cr. P.C. have been initiated as far as back on 10.01.2019, the High Court has just ignored the aforesaid relevant aspects and has granted anticipatory bail to respondent No. 2 - accused by observing that the nature of accusation is arising out of a business transaction.
The specific allegations of cheating, etc., which came to be considered by learned Additional Sessions Judge has not at all been considered by the High Court.
Even the High Court has just ignored the factum of initiation of proceedings under sections 82-83 of Cr. P.C. by simply observing that "be that as it may".
The aforesaid relevant aspect on grant of anticipatory bail ought not to have been ignored by the High Court and ought to have been considered by the High Court very seriously and not casually.

20. In the case of State of Madhya Pradesh v. Pradeep Sharma (Supra), it is observed and held by this court that if anyone is declared as an absconder/proclaimed offender in terms of section 82 of Cr. P.C., he is not entitled to relief of anticipatory bail."

entities.text: State of Madhya Pradesh v. Pradeep Sharma
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The present applicant, against whom process under Section 82 Cr.P.C. has been issued and who has been proclaimed as absconder, is not entitled for the benefit of the anticipatory bail in the light of the law laid down in Prem Shankar Prasad case (supra).
In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court, I deem it not a fit case to grant anticipatory bail to the present applicant.
Such a person, who does not cooperate with the investigation at all, is not entitled for any relief from this Court by way of granting anticipatory bail.
The anticipatory bail application is, accordingly, rejected.
